title: Consumer Deception & Hidden Costs
purpose: Track documented promotion restrictions and government-alleged or settled unfair/deceptive practices. This is an evidence register, not a guilt ranking or claim about a company's current conduct.

methodology.definition: Entries must cite first-party terms, a court/regulator complaint, an agency settlement or official refund record. One agency case can cover several allegations and one company may recur.
methodology.statusRules: Litigation allegations are not proven; a proposed settlement is not a final order; a consent settlement does not necessarily admit wrongdoing. Published restrictions can be lawful and should not be labeled deceptive without further evidence.
methodology.costRules: Do not sum settlement, fine or refund values as consumer losses or as one comparable series. Show event dates and amounts exactly as sourced, with proposed or settled qualifiers.
methodology.temporal: Historical allegations may describe past rather than current behavior; current checkout conditions need separate timestamped tests.
methodology.geo: National cases cannot be localized to a ZIP absent documented covered locations or location-specific price data. No personal customer details included.
methodology.sourcePolicy: Primary regulator and company sources preferred. Check procedural updates before describing open cases as decided.
methodology.sampling: Curated cases selected to illustrate diverse tactics, not a representative sample of all businesses or industries.
methodology.sourceVerification: FTC and company source URLs cross-checked on 2026-11-10 for high-impact examples; settlement status reflects stated court timeline as of that date. Continue case-status reviews, including official case pages, to detect later changes.

terms.name: Terms documented
terms.explanation: Terms and constraints are visible in company materials; no regulator deception finding.

lawsuit.name: Regulator allegations
lawsuit.explanation: Agency lawsuit filed; allegations remain to be resolved.

proposed.name: Proposed / announced settlement
proposed.explanation: Settlement announced or proposed; do not assume final court entry.

settlement.name: Settlement or refunds
settlement.explanation: Settlement documented, sometimes accompanied by distributed refunds; not necessarily an admission of wrongdoing.

tactics.name: Hidden mandatory fees
tactics.simple: The price grows after the consumer has already chosen.

tactics.name: Cancellation traps
tactics.simple: Signing up is easy, leaving or stopping charges is hard.

tactics.name: Restricted promotions
tactics.simple: Advertised benefits compete with restrictions revealed in terms.

tactics.name: Early-exit penalties
tactics.simple: A monthly headline conceals a longer commitment.

tactics.name: Service mismatch
tactics.simple: A headline service promise may not match actual delivery.

tactics.name: Bait pricing
tactics.simple: A low headline price allegedly cannot be bought as advertised.

tactics.name: Checkout mismatch
tactics.simple: The register charges more than the displayed price.

tactics.name: Misleading intermediaries
tactics.simple: A consumer thinks they're paying directly but pays a middleman.

tactics.name: Refund barriers
tactics.simple: Promised refund or protection can be difficult to obtain.

tactics.name: Service and contract traps
tactics.simple: Unexpected terms, extra charges and difficult exit hit business customers.

cases.name: T-Mobile / T-Mix
cases.headline: Two advertised upgrades can compete for one pool of benefits
cases.claim: Published T-Mix terms allocate device-promotion Picks at the account level. A two-line More plan has four shared Picks; a $1,200 promotion consumes three.
cases.mechanism: One account may not have enough Picks for both phones to claim the largest advertised deals, even though each line is eligible to shop offers.
cases.implication: Documented shared-promotion constraint; deception, financial injury, and legal violations have NOT been established.
cases.action: Ask for a written two-line, 36-month quote showing all Picks, promo conditions and credits.

cases.name: AT&T Mobility
cases.headline: Unlimited data was allegedly slowed after usage thresholds
cases.claim: FTC alleged the company failed to adequately disclose that some unlimited plans would be throttled after as little as 2 GB of data usage.
cases.mechanism: Customers continued paying for an unlimited plan but could experience severely reduced speeds.
cases.implication: 2019 $60 million FTC settlement. Refund activity continued into 2026.
cases.action: Compare disclosed prioritization/throttling thresholds and request written terms for any new plan.

cases.name: Amazon Prime
cases.headline: Prime enrollment and cancellation traps led to major settlement
cases.claim: FTC alleged millions were enrolled without consent and cancellation was deliberately difficult.
cases.mechanism: Recurring fees could continue unless consumers navigated difficult enrollment and cancellation paths.
cases.implication: 2025 $2.5 billion settlement; 2026 FTC reports more than $845 million paid in redress by September.
cases.action: Check subscriptions and refund eligibility through official FTC and Amazon channels; avoid refund solicitation scams.

cases.name: Progress Residential / Pretium Partners
cases.headline: Advertised rent allegedly left out mandatory monthly charges
cases.claim: FTC and four states alleged misleading advertised rents, hidden charges, disputed deposit deductions, move-in condition failures and service problems.
cases.mechanism: A renter comparing base rents may underestimate the monthly and move-out cost.
cases.implication: Proposed $49.75 million settlement with $48.5 million designated for consumer redress; final court approval not confirmed in this review.
cases.action: Request all required charges in writing, document move-in/out conditions and save itemized deposit records.

cases.name: Shutterstock
cases.headline: Automatic renewals and cancellation penalties inadequately disclosed
cases.claim: FTC alleged annual-paid-monthly renewal conditions and early-cancellation fees were obscured; some users were charged without informed consent.
cases.mechanism: A low displayed monthly price may hide a longer obligation and early-exit costs.
cases.implication: FTC announced proposed $35 million settlement; final court approval not established here.
cases.action: Check whether a plan is monthly or annual-paid-monthly and record the actual cancellation charge.

cases.name: Dollar General
cases.headline: FTC alleges shelf prices did not match register charges
cases.claim: FTC and 20 states sued over alleged repeated checkout overcharges relative to shelf, tag and advertising prices.
cases.mechanism: Small per-item discrepancies can accumulate across ordinary grocery and household purchases.
cases.implication: Active FTC/state lawsuit; no final liability decision identified.
cases.action: Compare scanned price to shelf price and preserve the receipt and shelf-tag photo.

cases.name: Uber One
cases.headline: Savings promises allegedly masked subscription costs and cancellation friction
cases.claim: FTC and states alleged enrollment without consent, advertised savings that omitted membership fees, and cancellation flows as long as 23 screens and 32 actions.
cases.mechanism: Customers may save less than advertised and pay unwanted recurring fees.
cases.implication: FTC/state amended complaint; allegations have not been adjudicated.
cases.action: Compare savings after membership fees; save cancellation confirmation and inspect following statements.

cases.name: StubHub
cases.headline: Ticket price display did not show complete mandatory fees up front
cases.claim: FTC charged that tickets were advertised without clear disclosure of mandatory fees until later in purchasing.
cases.mechanism: The ticket that appears cheapest can become more costly at checkout.
cases.implication: FTC announced $10 million settlement/refunds in April 2026.
cases.action: Compare the all-in price before purchasing and keep pre-checkout screenshots.

cases.name: Grubhub
cases.headline: Delivery price, subscription and worker earnings representations challenged
cases.claim: FTC and Illinois said consumers were misled about total delivery charges and subscription cancellation; settlement also addressed workers and unaffiliated restaurants.
cases.mechanism: A low menu/delivery price may be a poor proxy for the final order total.
cases.implication: $25 million payment under a court-entered settlement; FTC issued refunds in 2026.
cases.action: Compare checkout total and membership charges; use official FTC refund portal for program status.

cases.name: Adobe
cases.headline: Annual commitment sold with prominent monthly price
cases.claim: FTC/DOJ alleged a 50% remaining-payments early termination fee was inadequately disclosed and that cancellation was burdensome.
cases.mechanism: Customers may think they are buying a month-to-month subscription when they are committing to a year.
cases.implication: Regulator complaint; do not treat allegation as a proven violation.
cases.action: Find the contract duration and termination formula before purchasing a subscription.

cases.name: Lens.com
cases.headline: Advertised contact-lens prices allegedly doubled at checkout
cases.claim: FTC, Utah and Nevada alleged mandatory charges labeled taxes and fees were obscured and could routinely double the advertised lens price.
cases.mechanism: A product's advertised price becomes misleading for side-by-side comparison if mandatory charges appear only later.
cases.implication: FTC/state complaint; amounts are agency allegations, not audited aggregate consumer harm.
cases.action: Compare the total final order charge, not search-ad unit price, and preserve the full checkout.

cases.name: Toast
cases.headline: Restaurants allegedly faced unauthorized add-ons and difficult exits
cases.claim: FTC and states alleged hidden fees, costly cancellation terms, unauthorized add-ons, and customer-support promises not met.
cases.mechanism: Business operators may pay more or become locked into a service contract; some diner fees were also challenged.
cases.implication: FTC/state lawsuit; individual customer experiences and all alleged harms are not court findings.
cases.action: Request line-by-line processing and service fees, all exit terms, and payment-system access remedies.

cases.name: Stream Auto Outlet
cases.headline: Advertised vehicle prices allegedly understated actual purchase costs
cases.claim: FTC alleged that the Long Island dealership group advertised cars at low prices it would not honor.
cases.mechanism: Shoppers may invest travel and time in an offer that cannot be completed at the advertised price.
cases.implication: FTC announced agreement/proposed order in November 2026; court approval not established in this review.
cases.action: Obtain an out-the-door written quote including all mandatory dealer charges.

cases.name: Doxo
cases.headline: Search ads made a third-party bill-payment service look like the biller
cases.claim: FTC alleged deceptive search ads, add-on charges and unclear subscription enrollment; federal court found ROSCA violations.
cases.mechanism: Consumers may pay an intermediary and additional fees when they intended to pay their utility or another biller directly.
cases.implication: Court finding on subscription disclosures/consent; FTC announced proposed $2.1 million settlement.
cases.action: Navigate directly to the biller's official website and confirm payment destination.
cases.evidenceType: court finding and proposed FTC settlement

cases.name: GOAT
cases.headline: Buyer protection and expedited shipping did not always match promises
cases.claim: FTC alleged delayed shipments and failure to provide promised refunds for defective, incorrect or inauthentic items.
cases.mechanism: Shoppers may pay for speed or protection and then face extra friction recovering the purchase price.
cases.implication: FTC distributed more than $100,000 in 2026 refunds from a prior settlement.
cases.action: Keep delivery commitments and buyer-protection terms, file documented claim promptly.

cases.name: Ticketmaster / Live Nation
cases.headline: Ticket advertising and resale limits challenged
cases.claim: FTC and states alleged misleading lower advertised prices and claims of limits on ticket sales that professional brokers circumvented.
cases.mechanism: Ticket buyers may pay higher all-in resale prices and face constrained direct ticket availability.
cases.implication: Pending case; September 2026 order denied a motion to dismiss, which is not a decision on merits.
cases.action: Compare face-value, full fees and resale prices; distinguish original issue from resales.

cases.name: Riverside Payments / Cascade Equipment Leasing
cases.headline: Risk-free savings pitch allegedly turned into long contracts
cases.claim: FTC and Washington alleged misleading claimed savings and undisclosed automatic renewal plus equipment leasing restrictions.
cases.mechanism: A small business may become bound to equipment and processing contracts with costly exit terms.
cases.implication: Proposed $600,000 payment to resolve claims; much larger judgment partly suspended based on ability to pay.
cases.action: Demand separate hardware lease, auto-renewal and termination documents; preserve the sales proposal.

cases.name: Hopper
cases.headline: Travel app included preselected extras despite a 'no hidden fees' message
cases.claim: FTC alleged Hopper added Tip and VIP Support charges without informed consent and overstated price-freeze and support benefits; the federal court entered a $35 million settlement order in August 2026.
cases.mechanism: A quoted total may exclude preselected charges on the final screen, while add-on services may not provide their advertised protection.
cases.implication: Court-entered stipulated order; resolved allegations do not establish that every Hopper booking had these charges or that current practices remain the same.
cases.action: Before paying, inspect every preselected service and confirm the final price; save the booking and fee disclosures.
cases.evidenceType: FTC complaint and court-entered stipulated order

consumerActions.name: Price audit
consumerActions.detail: Compare advertisements with a screenshot of the all-in final price and all recurring charges.

consumerActions.name: Subscription audit
consumerActions.detail: Confirm contract length, renewal date, cancellation method, and written confirmation.

consumerActions.name: Wireless complaints
consumerActions.detail: Document service promises and screenshots before contacting the provider or filing an FCC billing/service complaint.

consumerActions.name: Refund eligibility
consumerActions.detail: Check official FTC refund programs; nobody should ask you to pay to receive an FTC refund.

consumerActions.name: Rent document review
consumerActions.detail: Ask for the full mandatory rent amount and keep signed documents and move-in/move-out photographs.
